Allows synchronization with the refresh rate of the monitor.
- Off: Do not synchronize. Frame rate is uncapped, but screen tearing might be more visible.
- On: Synchronize the presentation of frames with the monitor refresh rate. Eliminates tearing, but caps the frame rate at the monitor refresh rate. If the frame rate is lower than the monitor refresh rate, the frame rate will be capped further.
- VRR: Only available in Window and Fullscreen window modes with a monitor that supports VRR techniques (FreeSync, G-Sync, etc.). The monitor tries to match its refresh rate with the game refresh rate. Useful to eliminate tearing when the frame rate is less than the monitor refresh rate, but without capping.

This parameter is responsible for anti-aliasing, improving the final image. Temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) can significantly improve the quality of rendering, but it is recommended enabling it on stable and good FPS.

If the selected anti-aliasing mode supports upscaling, you can select the quality of the upscaling. Native means no upscaling, only anti-aliasing, while going for more performant presets results in rendering the game at a lower resolution, improving performance.
If the selected anti-aliasing mode supports sharpening, you can set the amount of sharpening. It’s not about image quality, it’s about your preference for image sharpness.

Controls the quality of shadows, including shadows of the terrain, moving objects, particle effects, and self-shadowing.
At lower values, the shadow will be rendered at a lower resolution, will be less accurate, and will have less detailed boundaries.
Additionally, lesser important objects (such as fences) will not form shadows at lower settings.

Controls the quality of the water, including water surface geometry, water reflections, and water foaming details.
At lower values, the water surface will have less details: waves will not have the heights and will be more pixelated, reflections will be less accurate (more blocky for terrain) and will include much less detail.

Controls the quality of the water effects, such as splashing (from bullets, bombs, etc...), boat trails, and water ripples.
At lower values, these effects will be less detailed and more pixelated.

Controls the quality of clouds while flying aircraft.
This includes the light scattering and transmitting accuracy, cloud blurriness and self-shadowing.
At lower settings, the clouds will feel less natural due to inaccurate scattering, will be blurrier and will have much less details.

Controls the quality of clouds while operating ground and naval vehicles.
It controls the resolution of the panorama view from the ground.

SSAO must be turned on if this setting is enabled.
If set to the lowest value, SSR is turned off.
If turned on, it improves all reflections, with increased quality based on the setting, against increased performance impact.

Controls the resolution of effects, including all kinds of smokes, explosions, earth splashes, flares, etc...
At lower values, these effects will be rendered with a lower resolution, causing them to be more pixelated and blurred.

Controls the quality of the landscape.
– 0: At the lowest value, the ground is just a texture with surface details.
– 1: On 1-3 settings, the ground will have a normal map, causing it to interact with light much more accurately, thus cracks will have textures, etc...
– 2: Terrain will have paralax effects in ground vehicles.
– 3: Terrain will have paralax effects in all vehicles.

Controls the SSAO (Screen Space Ambient Occlusion) quality, which means how detailed the self-shadowed on objects are.
– 0: SSAO is off, meaning that areas of objects that should receive less light will be brighter than they are supposed to be.
– 1: Uses standard SSAO.
– 2: Uses GTAO, which is much more accurate, but more demanding performance-wise.

Controls the quality of mirrors in the cockpit and X-ray simulation quality.
At the lowest settings, no images will appear in the cockpit mirrors. At higher settings, the resolution and detailedness of the mirrors will be increased.

Controls the global illumination model.
– Low: Global Illumination is mimicked by the directional lightning only.
– Medium: Global Illumination is turned on with one continuous bounce and uses brightness only by transmitted light.
– High: Global Illumination uses countinuous bounces, as well as colour and brightness by transmitted light.

Controls the quality of physics during the destruction of objects.
The lower the setting, the less accurate the simulation is, including destroyed parts clipping through objects, moving and rotating too quickly, etc...

Controls the quality of terrain displacement by explosions, bullets, etc...
The higher the setting the more detailed the height differences of the crater and bullet holes will be on the terrain.

Controls the resolution of the displacements on the earth from bombs, tracks, etc...
The main difference between this setting and “Terrain displacement quality” is that this setting controls the resolution of the texture, while “Terrain displacement quality” controls the quality of the height differences.
Controls the density of particles in after effects, such as explosions and splashes. The higher the value, the more particles there are.

Controls the distance from which grass will be rendered and the level of density.
At lower settings, barely any grass will be rendered. At higher values, the grass will be rendered at larger and larger distance, andin proximity to the player the grass will be denser and denser.

Controls the shadow quality on small details and objects.
The higher the value the smaller and smaller details can cast shadows.
It requires SSAO to be enabled.
Improves the quality of the shore texture and adds waves with foam on the shores.
Toggles whether to render a blurring distortion effect of hot air, for instance at the exhaust of a tank or aircraft engine, on top of fires, etc...
Improves the detailedness of the terrain at far distances, extending the clipmap quality from 4096 to 8192.
Toggles the lens flare effect. The lens flare effect mimics a real light phenomenon, when looking at bright lights you will see dim patters on the “lens” of the in-game camera.

Enables the use of ray tracing effects. It is recommended to use an upscaling anti-aliasing method (like DLSS, FSR, XeSS, or TSR) and choose an upscaling quality suitable for your GPU, as this option puts a heavy load on both the CPU and GPU.
To enable it, the use of Direct3D 12 or Vulkan graphics API and a ray tracing capable graphics card are required.
Controls how large the area covered by the ray tracing is. Affects the CPU performance and mainly affects the trees farther away from the camera.

Enables the use of ray traced ambient occlusion (RTAO) instead of screen space ambient occlusion (SSAO).
– Low: RTAO is rendered at half resolution and denoised using the performance profile.
– Medium: RTAO is rendered at full resolution and denoised using the performance profile.
–High: RTAO is rendered at full resolution and denoised using the quality profile.

Enables the use of ray traced shadows (RTSM) instead of the traditional shadow maps.
– Sun: RTSM is used for the sun only.
– Sun and dynamic: RTSM is used for the sun and all dynamic lights. Note that this method is very performance intensive!

Enables the use of ray traced reflections (RTR) instead of screen space reflections (SSR).
– Low: No RT shadows in the reflections, use a checkerboard pattern to improve performance, denoise using the performance profile.
– Medium: Use RT shadows in the reflections, use a checkerboard pattern to improve performance, denoise using the performance profile.
– High: Use RT shadows in the reflections, denoise using the performance profile.
– Ultra: Use RT shadows in the reflections, denoise using the quality profile.

Specify what resolution the ray traced reflections should be rendered in.
– Half: Reflections are rendered using half resolution both horizontally and vertically.
– Full: Reflections are rendered using the same resolution as the game.
Enables the use of ray traced reflections on water.

Specify what resolution the ray traced water reflections should be rendered in.
– Half: Reflections are rendered using half resolution both horizontally and vertically.
– Full: Reflections are rendered using the same resolution as the game.

Enables ray traced reflections on translucent glass surfaces.
– Medium: No RT shadows on reflections, rendered using half resolution both horizontally and vertically.
– High: Use RT shadows in the reflections, rendered using half resolution both horizontally and vertically.
Controls whether the display will mirror the left eye, right eye, or both eyes.
Removes the black borders (lens mask) around the image in Display Mirror. May reduce performance.

Specify what metrics to be displayed at the bottom left of the screen.
– Off: No performance metrics will be displayed.
– FPS: Graphics API and FPS will be displayed.
– Compact: A compacted version of FPS and Display Latency will be displayed.
